issue_context.title: incorrect tableDual plan which would cause no result
comments:
Problem comes from `excludeToIncludeForIntPoint` in detacher.go

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/c0fc3baf084ae3343328f30195c5e38f0fbe9ccf/pkg/util/ranger/detacher.go#L498C1-L500C5

When meeting a math.MaxInt64 for KindInt64 or 0 for KindUint64, simply an nil is returned.
 
Another corner case (0 for KindUint64) shows below:
```sql

CREATE TABLE `t5` (`d` int not null, `c` int not null, PRIMARY KEY (`d`, `c`));
CREATE TABLE `t6` (`d` bigint UNSIGNED not null);

insert into t5 values (-3, 6);
insert into t6 values (0), (1), (2), (3);

select * from t5 where d < (select min(d) from t6);

select * from t5 where d < (select min(d) from t6) and d < 3;

```

result follows (also can be reproduced on master branch):
```bash

mysql> select version();
+--------------------+
| version()          |
+--------------------+
| 8.0.11-TiDB-v7.5.1 |
+--------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)

mysql> select * from t5 where d < (select min(d) from t6);
+----+---+
| d  | c |
+----+---+
| -3 | 6 |
+----+---+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)

mysql> select * from t5 where d < (select min(d) from t6) and d < 3;
Empty set (0.01 sec)

mysql> explain select * from t5 where d < (select min(d) from t6) and d < 3;
+--------------+---------+------+---------------+---------------+
| id           | estRows | task | access object | operator info |
+--------------+---------+------+---------------+---------------+
| TableDual_31 | 0.33    | root |               | rows:0        |
+--------------+---------+------+---------------+---------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

The function should deal with the boundary value correctly. 

I guess it is not a bad idea to change the type of the point in this case.

Patch comes later

review_comments:
Seems that this function is only used to check whether the range is a point or not.
Why it will affect table dual or not?

> Seems that this function is only used to check whether the range is a point or not. Why it will affect table dual or not?

This function will convert the point to include mode. For example, input `c>9223372036854775807` will been changed to `c>=9223372036854775808`.
If an nil is returned, it means the condition is unsatisfiable. 

Hence the condition `c>9223372036854775807` with `c` (unsigned bigint) will return nil because of the bug.

This func is invoked in `allSinglePoints`. If nil is returned, it will simply skip this range(ignore unsatisfiable condition), the pos does not increase, which returns an empty slice.

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/d2eb9026a476dd76a3fbb9449834867c4ad2a87b/pkg/util/ranger/detacher.go#L533-L539

Function `allSinglePoints` has only been called inside `ExtractEqAndInCondition`, here an empty silce returned means the range is invalid and finally cause the TableDual Outside.

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/d2eb9026a476dd76a3fbb9449834867c4ad2a87b/pkg/util/ranger/detacher.go#L661-L670
So actual issue might be that: The range point may be Signed Int64 while the column is Unsigned Int64 or vice versa?

> So actual issue might be that: The range point may be Signed Int64 while the column is Unsigned Int64 or vice versa?

Yes.
If so, the comment should also be updated. Or we pass the column's field type to this function, to do a more accurate judgment.

> If so, the comment should also be updated. Or we pass the column's field type to this function, to do a more accurate judgment.

> @onlyacat Could you check this review？

Sorry for the late reply. 
Since this is just an early termination step, I guess it is not a bad idea to keep it simple and the unsatisfied value for specific field type will be eliminated in the later stage.
As for the comment, it described what I edited as actual. Not sure which should be updated.
